Rossland Museum & Discovery Centre · Draft for discussion · November 2026

A home for the Rossland Arena tractor

Simple ways to shelter and show the town's "Zamboni" on the museum grounds.

Short answer The Rink Corner Other options Side by side Cost Where to put it Fit with the renewal Ideas for the scene Next steps

The short answer

The Rink Corner is the best choice overall. It is a small board shed with a wide mesh front and a floor painted as ice.

It is the one new building here that locks the machine in and still shows its whole side.

The best place is beside the new entry path, built with the renewal site works. The upper grounds allow an earlier start.

Rossland snow makes any new roof costly. The Sea Can Garage costs about half as much. A spare bay under an existing roof costs least.

7.3 m wide, 4.3 m deep 24 ft by 14 ft
$55,000 to $80,000 rough cost with a contractor, before donations
Summer 2027 earliest opening on the upper grounds, with a decision by February

The Rink Corner Suggested

Drag to turn the model. Scroll or pinch to zoom.
  • Scene. The floor is white with a blue line. Rink boards line the back wall, under a photo of the arena stands. The garage doors are behind the tractor, as if it just rolled out.
  • View. The tractor is at a slight angle. Visitors see the Ford face and the whole side.
  • Protection. The walls and doors are solid. Black welded mesh closes the front, and air moves through it. Board shutters, painted as rink boards, lock over the mesh for winter.
  • Structure. The roof rests on the two end walls, so the wide front opening holds up almost no roof. A long beam is not necessary.
  • Moving in. The machine drives in through the garage doors.
Size 7.3 m wide, 4.3 m deep (24 ft by 14 ft)Rough cost $55,000 to $80,000Time on site 5 to 7 weeks

Clear plastic sheet (polycarbonate) can replace one or two mesh panels for cleaner photos. It needs washing, and it shows reflections.

The shed takes its board walls, red trim and metal roof from the grounds, and its door colours from the arena garage.

Other options

The Garage

Its little garage home, nose to the gate.

  • The tractor faces out through mesh gates, as in the Tourism Rossland garage photo.
  • Solid doors close over the gates for winter.
  • Visitors see the nose. A mesh window in the side shows the resurfacer.
Size 4.3 m wide, 7.3 m deepRough cost $55,000 to $85,000Time on site 5 to 7 weeks

The Sea Can Garage

A used steel container, clad to look like the garage.

  • A 20 ft container, clad in boards. The steel doors open on a mesh gate, and lock shut for winter.
  • It can go in before the renewal works end, and move later.
  • The fit is tight: about 2.35 m inside for a machine about 2.1 m wide.
  • The City must allow a container there. The cost allows for a light roof over it, in case the engineer asks for one.
Size 2.4 m wide, 6.1 m deepRough cost $20,000 to $40,000Time on site 2 to 3 weeks

The Centre Ice Pavilion

An open timber roof over a raised slab painted as ice.

  • A larger twin of the Esso pump canopy. It is the best match with the older buildings.
  • Visitors see the machine from all four sides.
  • A rail does not stop a climber, and blown snow gets to the machine.
Size 7.3 m wide, 4.9 m deepRough cost $45,000 to $70,000Time on site 4 to 6 weeks

The Borrowed Roof

A mesh enclosure under a roof the museum already has.

  • A white floor and a mesh enclosure go under an existing shelter. The museum builds no roof.
  • It needs a spare bay that a truck can get to, such as one in the fire hall.
  • The tractor shares the space with another story.
Size 5.6 m by 3.2 m enclosureRough cost $8,000 to $20,000Time on site 1 to 2 weeks

Cost

Snow sets the price. A Rossland roof must hold about 115 pounds of snow on each square foot.

The ranges are rough, in 2026 dollars, for work by a contractor. The engineer and the permit are in the price. So are the concrete floor, the apron, the building and the scene inside. They leave out the move, a path to the spot and the story panel.

Before work starts on site, the engineer, the permit and the roof trusses take 10 to 14 weeks. Concrete needs bare ground.

Ways to bring it down

  • The renewal contractor could price the floor and shed with the site works.
  • Local businesses could sponsor the rink boards. Each board shows a name, as at the arena.
  • Local trades and suppliers could give labour and lumber.
  • The City could give old boards, signs and tools from the arena.

Where to put it

The renewal drawing of the new entrance.

The museum's current map, drawn before the renewal. The pins are approximate.

  • 1Beside the new entry path. This is the nearest thing to having it indoors. Every visitor passes it, staff can see it, and power is close. The lawn slopes. The spot needs a level pad. The renewal designers know where the new atrium and ramp leave room.
  • 2Upper grounds, by the Esso pumps. It joins the trucks and automobiles, clear of the renewal works. It is out of sight of the building. A Sea Can Garage can start here and move to pin 1 later.
  • 3Under an existing roof. This suits the Borrowed Roof, if the fire hall or another shelter has a bay to spare.

Each spot needs a straight approach for the truck that delivers the machine.

Fit with the renewal

  • Look. Beside the atrium, the shed can take the renewal's horizontal wood and dark trim. On the upper grounds, board walls and red trim match the older buildings.
  • Site works. A level pad, a power conduit and a path cost least as part of the renewal site works.
  • Timing. A spot beside the entry path follows the renewal schedule. The Sea Can Garage, or a spare bay, can hold the machine until then.
  • Story. The tractor belongs to Rossland hockey. The Sports Hall of Fame inside can send visitors out to it.
  • Money. Sponsored boards and donated work can pay for it apart from the renewal campaign.

Ideas for the scene

Not a Zamboni

For about 40 years, a Ford farm tractor made the ice at the Rossland Arena.

In 2012 the City planned to retire it. A short film, The Flood, drew more than 50,000 views in two weeks, and the tractor stayed.

A possible opening for the story panel.

  • Sponsor names on the rink boards.
  • A red goal light, and an old scoreboard or bench sign from the arena.
  • The drivers' names inside the garage doors.
  • A QR code that opens The Flood on a phone.
  • A tractor seat and steering wheel outside, for children and photos.
  • Shutters open for Winter Carnival.

Next steps

  1. Measure the machine: length, width, height and weight. The drawings use estimates.
  2. Choose the option and the place, with the renewal designers.
  3. Ask the City if a development permit applies, and if it allows a container.
  4. Hire a structural engineer, then get quotes from two local contractors.
  5. Apply for the building permit and order the materials.
  6. Build when the ground is clear of snow, then move the machine in.

The Borrowed Roof needs steps 1 and 2 only, then a mesh supplier.

Numbers for the builder

  • Rossland Building Bylaw 2716, Appendix B, gives the ground snow load by area: 5.6 kPa (Redstone), 6.8 kPa (Main Rossland), 7.2 kPa (Red Mountain Base).
  • The same table gives 0.1 kPa for rain, 0.35 kPa for wind, and a footing depth of 36 inches.
  • The bylaw exempts accessory buildings under 10 square metres from a permit. Each new building here is larger.
  • The tractor is a Ford 3000. Published figures give 3.2 m long, 1.6 m wide and 2.1 m to the top of the exhaust.
  • With the resurfacer, the estimate from photos is 4.5 to 5.0 m long and 2.1 m wide. The drawings allow 5.0 m by 2.2 m, and up to 3,200 kg.

Not yet confirmed

  • The costs are rough estimates, not quotes. The Sea Can Garage figure is the least certain.
  • The container option needs checks on the fit, the roof under snow and City zoning.
  • The renewal site plan decides the exact spot beside the entry path.
  • The drawings and the 3D model show the idea and the main sizes. They are not construction drawings.
